pros: Free plan includes unlimited event types and bookings for individuals
Can be self-hosted, with the full source code open to audit
Embeddable components and API let you build scheduling into your own product
Round robin, collective events and routing forms on the team plan
cons: Frequent releases bring occasional rough edges and moved settings
Self-hosting needs engineering time and some features still need a licence
CRM routing and large-org admin controls trail Calendly
verdict_line: Pick Cal.com if you need to self-host scheduling or embed it inside your own product.

pros: Bookings create and update Zoho CRM records without connector work
Service, staff and resource model suits clinics, salons and multi-location businesses
Included in Zoho One and priced low per staff member otherwise
Admin can book on behalf of walk-in and phone customers
cons: Booking pages look plainer and take more steps than Calendly or SavvyCal
No weighted round robin, routing forms or CRM ownership lookup for sales
Non-Zoho integrations mostly rely on Zoho Flow or Zapier
verdict_line: Pick Zoho Bookings if your business already runs on Zoho CRM and needs staff and service appointment booking.

pros: Intake forms per appointment type with required and conditional questions
Sells packages, gift certificates, subscriptions and memberships natively
Deposits or full payment at booking through Stripe, Square or PayPal
Classes and group sessions with capacity limits alongside one-on-one bookings
Multi-staff and multi-location calendars at a small business price
cons: No free plan, only a short trial
No routing forms, CRM lookup or weighted round robin for sales teams
Admin and client-facing design looks dated next to newer tools
Integrations beyond calendars, video and payments mostly go through Zapier
verdict_line: Pick Acuity Scheduling if you sell appointments and need intake forms, packages and payment at booking.

pros: Recipients overlay their own calendar to pick a time that works for both
Personalised links and plain language pages make a good impression
Ranked availability and weekly meeting limits protect your best hours
HubSpot integration logs meetings and creates contacts natively
cons: No free plan, and per user pricing matches Calendly's paid tiers
Limited Salesforce depth and thin admin tooling for large teams
Overlay only works when the recipient grants calendar access
verdict_line: Pick SavvyCal if the impression your booking link makes on senior prospects and investors matters.

pros: Schedules tasks into calendar gaps and replans automatically when meetings move
Tasks, projects and calendar live in one view for small teams
Booking pages respect protected focus time and task deadlines
Workload view shows whether an assignee can hit a deadline
cons: Booking pages lack routing forms, weighted round robin and CRM lookup
Automatic planning only works if every task has honest durations and deadlines
No free plan and per user pricing is high for an individual
Admin controls and reporting are thin for larger organisations
verdict_line: Pick Motion if you want your own tasks planned onto the calendar automatically, not just external bookings.
